reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it covers President Kovind laying the foundation stone for the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial and Cultural Centre in Lucknow, with footage attributed to Doordarshan. The formal ceremony, officials, monks, dignitary speaking at a lectern, and applauding audience are consistent with public-event coverage. The visible channel subscription prompt is ordinary audience engagement and is not tied to payment, credentials, investment participation, or a benefit offer.

President Kovind lays foundation stone of Bharat Ratna Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial and Cultural Centre at Lucknow on June 29, 2021.

opening.argument: The description pairs an explicit viewer action, “Subscribe Now,” with an external shortened URL: “https://goo.gl/XUQgqi.” That is a direct action pathway presented before the event description, and the audience is also urged to “Stay Updated!” Although no reward is stated, the combination leaves open a low-barrier acquisition or claim funnel that the available material does not explain or rule out. The judge should therefore treat the link-and-subscribe pairing as a solicitation signal rather than automatically as ordinary reporting.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the footage ceremonial does not answer the separate solicitation embedded in the description. The title and event description establish the topic, but they do not explain what the shortened URL provides or why viewers should subscribe. A legitimate event can still be used to attract clicks, so the public-event setting does not by itself eliminate the possibility of a low-barrier acquisition flow.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action is only a subscription prompt, and the supplied text contains no reward, payment request, registration, deposit, or promised benefit. The URL is not described as a claim or verification flow. The argument identifies a link but cannot show the required reward-action relationship, while the event description identifies the video as coverage of a dated public ceremony.

opening.argument: Several engagement signals appear together: “Subscribe Now,” “Stay Updated!”, a shortened external link, and multiple additional social-media and website links. The description also repeats a channel-subscription instruction. This concentration of off-platform pathways can direct viewers away from the event itself and toward actions whose purpose is not stated. Even without a visible payment demand, the combination is sufficiently unexplained that a low-barrier acquisition or verification concern is not ruled out.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the subscription prompt as routine, but it does not account for the shortened link or the cluster of external destinations. The supplied description places these calls to action prominently alongside the event summary. Formal visuals may establish a setting, yet they cannot establish what viewers encounter after following the link or whether the calls to action serve a separate promotional funnel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited links are identified as official social accounts, an official channel, and an official website; the text does not promise money, assets, gifts, or easy returns for visiting them. A shortened link is unexplained, but unexplained is not evidence of a scam mechanism. The visuals show a public ceremony, not a financial or acquisition offer, so the alleged combination remains speculative.

citations.quote: Follow The President of India: ►Twitter: https://twitter.com/rashtrapatibhvn ►Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/PresidentOfIndia/ ►Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/presidentofindia/

opening.argument: The material can be read as promotional distribution rather than purely informational coverage. The description opens with “Subscribe Now,” tells viewers to “Stay Updated!”, and then supplies links to Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, a channel, and a website. Those calls to action surround the event account and encourage continued audience participation. The event framing may lend institutional credibility to the promotion, while the precise benefit of subscribing or following is not stated, leaving a low-barrier acquisition concern unresolved.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense assumes that formal scenery determines the role of the entire upload. But the description itself begins with a subscription command and distributes viewers across several destinations. Attribution to Doordarshan may describe the footage, yet it does not establish that every surrounding call to action is merely neutral news context. The institutional presentation could instead make the promotional pathway appear more trustworthy.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description expressly identifies the subject as the President laying a foundation stone and attributes the video to Doordarshan. The links are labeled as official social accounts and an official website, not as a purchase, investment, claim, or income opportunity. Promotional audience engagement may exist, but this argument still cannot connect it to a promised reward or acquisition.
